subject: Multi-region Dedicated — bundling, staged commit, and DR pricing questions
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@skybound.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@skybound.ai
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Multi-region Dedicated — capacity & DR pricing questions

Hi Marcus,

We’re kicking off a vendor selection for a Dedicated inference platform and Redwood is in the short list. A couple of key asks from our platform and procurement teams:

- We need separate reserved GPU pools in us-east-1 and us-west-2 (no shared failover by default) but want the option to enable active replication for DR with near-instant failover.
- What does a staged commit look like? We’d prefer pilot credits -> regional commits -> global commit conversion.
- Throughput guarantees: target 600 p50 QPS and 750 p95 per region during steady state. Can you support 99.9% token-level availability and per-route latency SLOs?
- Pricing/discount asks: looking for a 1-year and 3-year committed model. Procurement prefers a single PO that covers multi-region commit and an add-on for replication/replication storage.

Attached is our 12-month forecast for peak/avg QPS by region. Also share: preferred approach for cross-region routing cost, incremental GPU pool sizing guidance, and any recommended guardrails for autoscaling bursts.

Thanks — happy to set a 30-min sync next week.

Elena Morales
Head of Platform
Skybound AI

[Attachment: Skybound_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (1.2MB)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@skybound.ai>, procurement@skybound.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated — capacity & DR pricing questions

Elena — thanks for the clear brief and the forecast. Quick clarifying questions and a suggested packaging approach below.

Clarifying Qs:
- Can you confirm steady-state token length distribution (short vs long sequences) — that drives kernel selection and effective throughput?
- Are you planning geo-aware routing (client chooses nearest) or will you want Redwood to route across regions for resilience?
- RTO/RPO target for failover (e.g., RTO < 5m, RPO < 1h)?

Suggested packaging (initial proposal):
1) Pilot (30 days) — pilot credits that cover the expected steady-state token volume for a single region + ops assistance.
2) Regional reserved commits — 12-month commit per region sized to 120% of your steady-state QPS (to allow bursts).
3) Replication / DR add-on — optional priced as a percent uplift on committed spend plus per-GPU-hour for replicated standby capacity. We typically price active replication at ~15% of committed pool cost for warm-standby configuration (lower if replication is cold).
4) Cross-region routing — small per-request routing fee when we proxy across regions; can be waived for initial 30-day pilot.

Discount thinking: committed spend tiers (example): 10–25% off retail depending on term and total committed spend; we can firm numbers after your confirmed forecast and desired term.

I attached an early pricing sketch and a short SOW that outlines the staged-commit conversion flow. If you’re available Tues/Wed next week I’ll bring Soojin and Karthik to run the numbers and alignment.

—Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RDW_multi-region_pricing_v1.pdf (420KB)]

From: Elena Morales <elena@skybound.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@skybound.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated — capacity & DR pricing questions

Thanks Marcus — answers inline below and some follow-ups.

- Token lengths: median ~24 tokens, tail up to 480 tokens for complex multi-step flows.
- Routing: we prefer client-side geo-routing by default but require automatic cross-region failover for health events.
- RTO/RPO: target RTO <= 3 minutes for critical routes, RPO <= 15 minutes.

Numbers (per region):
- us-east-1 steady: 600 p50 / 750 p95
- us-west-2 steady: 180 p50 / 240 p95
- expected peak burst factor: 2.5x for shopping events (seasonal)

Procurement asks: please provide 1-year and 3-year committed pricing with clear breakouts: committed pool cost, replication add-on (if enabled), routing fees, and an annualized discount schedule. For 3-year we’re asking for deeper discounts — procurement’s target is ~25% off list for a multi-region package if we do a consolidated PO.

I’m attaching we’ve also included our procurement standard terms so legal can review earlier in the process.

Elena

[Attachment: SkyProcurement_Terms.pdf (240KB)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 13:37:00 +0000
Subject: INTERNAL: Skybound pricing approaches and redline risks

Marcus — internal note before we reply to procurement. Key points and recommendations: 

- Discount bands: recommend
  * 1-year: 18% off list for consolidated 2-region commit (min $X/month spend)
  * 3-year: 25% off list for consolidated commit (commit floors to be negotiated)
- Replication pricing: two options
  * Warm-standby (recommended): replicate KV + prefix caching, charged as 12–18% uplift on committed spend + per-GPU-hour for active warm nodes during failover testing.
  * Cold-standby: snapshot-based failover with storage and rehydration costs only (lower price but longer RTO).
- Cross-region routing: waive routing fees for first 30 days of pilot; afterwards charge a nominal per-request fee or include it in the replication uplift for large commits.
- Staged commit mechanics: pilot credits -> conversion window (30 days post-pilot) where credits translate to reserved commit at an agreed multiplier (we suggest 0.9x conversion factor to cover pilot subsidization).
- Legal redlines: procurement is likely to push for strict uptime credits and data residency language. Ask legal to prepare a template amendment that caps SLA credits to a percentage of monthly committed spend (standard: 10–20%).

Can Karthik and Rishi confirm: 1) whether 12–18% uplift looks defensible for warm-standby across N1/8 and A100 equivalent pools; 2) whether we can commit to a 3-minute RTO for warm-standby without increased premium?

If we’re comfortable I’ll draft the 1-pager for procurement with the two term options and attach the SOW for signatures.

— Soojin

[Internal — do not forward]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated — bundling, staged commit, and DR pricing questions

Elena / Procurement team — thanks for the details and the procurement doc. Below is a concise proposal and next steps based on our internal alignment.

Summary proposal (high level):
1) Pilot — 30 days, single region (us-east-1) covered by Redwood credits to validate latency, autoscaling behavior, and failover. Cross-region routing fees waived during pilot.
2) Regional reserved commits — 12-months per region priced as follows (examples):
   - us-east-1: commit sized to 120% of steady-state -> baseline price at list $Y/month -> 18% discount for 12-month consolidated PO
   - us-west-2: smaller commit sized similarly -> included in consolidated pricing
3) Replication (Warm-standby) add-on — optional. Pricing: 15% uplift on committed spend + per-GPU-hour for active failover use. Guarantees: target RTO <= 3 minutes for warm-standby test scenarios (we’ll include runbook and quarterly DR exercises).
4) 3-year option: 25% discount on list for consolidated 3-year commit with contractual floors and annual review for capacity adjustments.

Operational notes:
- We’ll provide per-route latency SLOs and token-level availability targets in the SOW.
- Staged commit conversion: pilot credits will be convertible to reserved credits within 30 days of pilot completion at a 0.9 conversion factor (to account for pilot subsidy).
- Single PO supported. Billing will be centralized by account; we’ll include separate line items for replication and routing for transparency.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached a short SOW and the pricing sheet for your review. Please confirm whether procurement prefers 12- or 36-month term and we’ll issue a formal quote and DocuSign.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/SBD-2026-314

Marcus Lin
